parts.title: Getting Started
parts.desc: Everything you need to know before you begin using NEOS.

blocks.text: NEOS is a comprehensive application designed to help manage and analyze patient authorizations, claims, and transactions over the patient lifecycle. It provides tools for tracking and reviewing data related to these workflows, ensuring efficient E5 workflow management across your organization.
NEOS is accessed through the Automation Hub and is designed to work across a range of devices including tablets, desktops, laptops, and other compatible devices.

items: Log in to Automation Hub — Navigate to the Automation Hub and log in with your credentials.
Locate the NEOS icon — Once logged in, look for the NEOS icon in the left panel of the Automation Hub.
Click to open — The Dashboard is the default landing page after login.

blocks.cap: NEOS icon in the Automation Hub left panel

items: What devices support NEOS?
NEOS supports Tablet, Desktop, Laptop, and other compatible devices.
How do I report a bug or request a feature?
Contact the support team via the Support icon within the application or by emailing support@e5.ai.
What do I do if I receive an error message?

Follow the instructions provided in the error message. Common errors include network issues, authentication problems, or data loading failures. If the issue persists, contact Element5 support for further assistance.
How do I exit NEOS and return to the Automation Hub?
Close the NEOS window in your browser to return to the Automation Hub.

parts.title: Global Features
parts.desc: Platform tools that work consistently across Authorization, Claims, and all future NEOS modules.

intro.text: The features in this section are available throughout the entire NEOS platform. They work the same way whether you are in the Authorization module, the Claims module, or any future module added to NEOS. Learn them once and apply them everywhere.

blocks.text: Review Mode enables users to focus on unresolved tasks by filtering out completed items, showing only those that require attention. This streamlines workflows by helping your team prioritize action items, improving efficiency and ensuring no critical tasks are overlooked.
Review Mode is available in all Authorization and Claims views. Enable it by clicking the Review Mode toggle in the top right of any view within the relevant module.

blocks.cap: Review Mode toggle in the top right of the view

items: Select a view — Navigate to any Authorization or Claims Center view — Dashboards, Auth Request View, Patient Auth Summary View, Claims Batch View, or Claims Status View.
Enable Review Mode — Click the Review Mode toggle. The view will immediately filter to show only records requiring your attention.
Work through your queue — Records are automatically filtered and sorted, highlighting those that need action. Focus on critical tasks without distraction.
Mark items as reviewed — Check the Reviewed? checkbox next to any record once you have actioned it. The item drops off the Review Mode list immediately.
Toggle off — Turn Review Mode off at any time to return to the full unfiltered view.
Auth Status — Partially Approved, Denied, Pending (>10 days), Exceptions
AT Status — Needs Attention, Needs Intervention
Patient Summary — Expiring episodes, Expiring auths
Batch View — Rejected batches, Batch Exceptions
Claims Status — Payor Rejected, Exceptions, Timely Filing Untimely
AT Status — Needs Attention, Needs Intervention

blocks.text: Once a record is marked as reviewed it cannot be unchecked. Only records that have not yet been reviewed will be pulled into this view when the feature is toggled on to allow attention only on items still requiring end user attention.

Sorting and filtering tools are available across all NEOS views and dashboards, giving you precise control over the data you see. Filters applied globally persist as you move between views within a module.
Sorting helps you organize data in a meaningful way, making it easier to find the information you need.

items: Click any column header to sort the data by that column in ascending order.
Click again to toggle between ascending and descending order.
Combine with filters — apply filters first to narrow down the data, then sort to organize the results for easier analysis.

blocks.text: Global Level Filters are applied across all views and dashboards within a module, providing consistent filtering across different sections.

items: Access filters — Click the Add More Filters button at the top of any view to open the filter panel.
Select filter fields — Choose from available attributes such as Payor Type, Gateway, Branch, Payor Source, and Mode.
Set values — Select one or more values for each filter field.
Add more criteria — Click Add More within the filter menu to stack multiple filter conditions.
Apply — Click Apply Filter. The filter will take effect across all views within the module.
Remove a filter — Click the X next to any active filter chip, or clear all criteria and click Apply Filter.

blocks.cap: Auth Initiated Date and Add More Filters panel

blocks.text: The Auth Initiated Date (Authorization) and Claim Init. Date (Claims) filters persist as you navigate between views within a module.

Available in Authorization views. When checked, authorization transactions that do not warrant a portal request are removed from the details grid and summary counts adjust automatically. When Review Mode is active, this checkbox becomes greyed out and non-clickable.

Every view includes a Search Patient Records bar that searches across key identifiers. In Authorization views you can search by patient name, E5 ID, MRN, Episode ID, or Member ID. In Claims views you can also search by Claim ID.

The Automation Log is available within every NEOS module and displays a comprehensive list of all automation transactions for the workflows in that module. It gives you full visibility into each step of the workflow lifecycle — including transaction IDs, workflow names, current stages, and automation outcomes.

Use the Automation Log to investigate workflow failures, review retry history, and understand why a transaction ended up in a Needs Attention or Needs Intervention state. Access it via the Automation Log tab within any module's center view.

blocks.text: The Claims Automation Log includes an additional field: Batch E5 ID (the parent batch identifier). This is specific to the Claims module. All other fields and behaviors are identical.

items: What is the difference between Terminated and Failed?

Terminated — Needs Attention means the automation stopped based on a business rule after exhausting all retry attempts. Failed — Needs Attention means a technical issue caused the transaction to fail. Both require human review but for different reasons — Terminated items are business exceptions while Failed items are technical exceptions.
How do I find all transactions for a specific patient or batch?

Use the Search Patient Records bar in the Automation Log to search by patient name, MRN, Member ID, or E5 ID. In the Claims module you can also search by Batch E5 ID to find all transactions associated with a specific batch.

blocks.text: The Reporting feature gives your team direct access to NEOS workflow data — enabling you to extract, filter, and analyze records outside of the platform. Reports are generated on demand and delivered securely via email, ready for download and further analysis in the tool of your choice.

The Reports icon is always visible in the top-right corner of the NEOS navigation bar, regardless of which screen or workflow you are currently working in. You never need to navigate away from your current task to generate a report.

items: Flexible Filtering: Apply date range, gateway, branch, and payer source filters to scope your report precisely to the data that matters.
Customizable Fields: Select only the data fields relevant to your analysis using simple toggle checkboxes.
On-Demand Generation: Generate reports at any time from any screen in NEOS without disrupting your current workflow.
Secure Email Delivery: Reports are delivered via a secure, time-limited email link — ready for download within minutes.
Locate the Reports icon — Look for the Reports icon in the top-right corner of the NEOS navigation bar. It is always visible regardless of which screen you are on. Click it to get started.

blocks.cap: Reports icon in the top-right navigation bar

items: Open the Reporting panel — A slide-out panel will appear from the right side of the screen. This panel layers over your current view so you never lose your place in NEOS. Review the available sections before making selections.
Select a process — Click the process selector and choose the process you want to report on (e.g. Authorizations). This tells the system which workflow dataset to pull from.
Apply filters — Apply one or more filters to refine the data included in your report. You can use any combination of filters or leave them at their defaults for a broader dataset.
Select fields — Scroll to the field selection area. Use the checkboxes next to each field to toggle them on or off. Checked fields will appear as columns in the generated report.

blocks.cap: Reporting panel — process, filters, and field selection

items: Generate the report — Click Generate Report at the bottom of the panel. The system will begin compiling your report. An on-screen acknowledgment confirms the report is in progress. You can close the panel and continue working while the report is prepared.
Download via email — When your report is ready you will receive an automated email to your registered address containing a secure download link. Click the link to download the file immediately.

rows: Specify the time period for the report.
Filter by authorization or claims gateway.
Narrow results to specific branch locations.
Filter by records assigned to a specific payor.
Narrow records by service line with applicable processes.
Narrow claim records by claim type.

blocks.text: The secure download link in your email is valid for 30 minutes from the time it is sent. If the link expires before you access it, return to NEOS, reopen the Reports panel, reapply your settings, and click Generate Report again to receive a new link.

items: How long does it take to receive my report?

Reports are typically ready within minutes of generation. You will receive an automated email to your registered address when the report is ready for download. The delivery time can vary based on the size of the data extracted from the system.
What happens if my download link expires?
Secure download links are valid for 30 minutes. If your link expires, return to NEOS, reopen the Reports panel, reapply your settings, and click Generate Report to receive a new link.
Can I access the Reports panel from any screen?
Yes — the Reports icon is always visible in the top-right navigation bar regardless of which screen or module you are currently working in. You do not need to navigate away from your current task.

parts.title: Managing Authorizations in NEOS
parts.desc: Managing patient authorizations, tracking requests, and monitoring automation outcomes.

intro.text: Review Mode, Sort & Filter, Automation Log, and Reporting all apply to this module — see Part II: Global Features for full guidance on each.

blocks.text: The Authorization Dashboard is your starting point each day. It provides a comprehensive view of key authorization metrics, trend data, and actionable items — giving your team immediate visibility into what needs attention.
Access the Dashboard by clicking the NEOS tab in the side panel of the Automation Hub, or by selecting the Authorization sub-tab at the top of any NEOS screen.

Action Items: Lists Payor Auth Request and response tasks requiring immediate attention, plus Automation Action Items where the automation could not complete the lifecycle. All items are clickable and navigate directly to the relevant records.

How do I view Action Items?
Click on any item under the Action Items section. This navigates you directly to the relevant subset of records in the Authorization views.
What happens when I complete an Action Item?
Once an Action Item is marked as reviewed in the Authorization view, it will disappear from the Action Items list and no longer be pulled into Review Mode.

parts.title: Managing Claims in NEOS
parts.desc: Managing claim submissions, tracking batches through the clearinghouse pipeline, and monitoring payor responses.

intro.text: Review Mode, Sort & Filter, Automation Log, and Reporting all apply to this module — see Part II: Global Features for full guidance on each.

blocks.text: The Claims module is a dedicated workspace within NEOS that gives your team full visibility into every claim submitted on behalf of your patients. Claims lives in its own top-level tab alongside Authorization, accessible from the main NEOS navigation bar.

At its core, Claims tracks each submission through a three-stage pipeline — from the moment a batch is transmitted, through clearinghouse validation, and ultimately to payor-level acceptance and payment.

items.d: Confirms whether a submitted batch was successfully received and accepted or rejected at the clearinghouse level.
Tracks clearinghouse-level acceptance or rejection of individual claims before they are forwarded to the payor.
Reflects the payor's final response — whether the claim is pending, accepted, rejected, or flagged as an exception.

blocks.text: NEOS handles several distinct claim types, each representing a different point in the patient care and billing process.

items.d: Hospice-specific notification submitted to Medicare when a patient elects hospice care. Required to initiate the hospice billing period. Not a payment claim.
Hospice-specific notification submitted to Medicare when a patient's hospice election ends. Required to close the care period for billing.
Home health-specific notification submitted to Medicare at the start of a home health episode. Required before a final claim can be submitted.
The actual billing claim submitted to the payor requesting payment for services rendered. Contains a full service line breakdown.

blocks.text: NOE, NOTR, and NOA are Medicare notifications, not payment requests. They carry their own timely filing requirements and will surface as action items if submissions fall outside the required window.

Timely filing refers to the requirement that certain claim types — particularly NOE, NOTR, and NOA notifications — must be submitted within a five-day window from the relevant event date. NEOS tracks this automatically and flags any claims approaching or past their deadline.
Claims flagged as Untimely indicate submissions that did not meet the required filing window. These should be reviewed and actioned promptly to avoid compliance issues.

The Claims Dashboard is your starting point each day for the Claims module. It provides a consolidated view of batch and claim-level performance, surfacing trends, filing compliance, and items requiring your immediate attention.
Access by selecting the Claims tab in the main navigation, then ensuring the Claims sub-tab is active alongside the Authorization sub-tab.

items: Batch Status Summary: A snapshot of all batches submitted — total batches, clearinghouse-accepted, clearinghouse-rejected, and batch exceptions.
Claim Status Summary: A claim-level breakdown tracking individual claims across all three pipeline stages.

Claim Level Trends: Visual charts including claim level status over time, claim type distribution by volume or value, payor type distribution, submission and charge trends, and the Timely Filing Tracker.
Action Items Panel: Divided into Claims Action Items (outcome-based) and Automation Action Items (workflow issues). All items are clickable and navigate directly to the relevant records.

Batches not successfully submitted to the clearinghouse. Require review and resubmission.
Batches where an issue occurred at the transmission level and did not reach the clearinghouse. Distinct from claim-level exceptions.

items: NOE / NOA / NOTR Filing — Untimely: Notifications submitted outside the required five-day window.
Payor Rejections: Claims forwarded to the payor that the payor subsequently rejected.
Batch Exceptions: Batches where a transmission-level issue prevented normal processing.
Batch Rejections: Batches not accepted by the clearinghouse.

blocks.text: All action items are clickable — selecting any item navigates directly to the subset of records carrying that status in the Claims Center.
HOW TO USE THE CLAIMS DASHBOARD

items: Review Action Items first — Prioritise untimely filing flags and payor rejections — these carry the most immediate compliance and revenue risk.
Adjust the date range — Use the Claim Init. Date filter to expand or narrow the time window.
Analyze trends — Use the Claim Level Trends charts to understand submission volume, claim type distribution, and timely filing performance.
Drill into records — Click any action item count or summary status to navigate to that specific subset of records in the Claims Center to review or provide needed interventions.

blocks.text: Click Add More Filters to open the filter panel. Select a Filter Field and corresponding values, then click Apply Filter. Filters apply across the entire Claims Dashboard for the selected date range.

items: What is the difference between a Batch Rejection and a Payor Rejection?
A Batch Rejection means the entire batch was not successfully submitted or accepted by the clearinghouse — the claims never reached the payor or system of processing.
A Payor Rejection means the batch was accepted by the clearinghouse and claims were forwarded to the payor, but the payor rejected them upon review.
Batch Rejections should be investigated at the batch level in the Batch View. Payor Rejections require individual claim-level review in the Claims Status View.
What is a Batch Exception versus a general Exception?

A Batch Exception relates to an issue with the transmission of the batch file itself. A general Exception (visible in the Payor stage of the Claims Status View) relates to individual patient claim records within the claim statusing flow.
What does Timely Filing mean and what should I do when I see an Untimely flag?
Timely Filing refers to the requirement that certain claim types must be submitted within a five-day window from the relevant event date.
When you see an Untimely flag, review the record and take appropriate follow-up action. These items also appear in the Action Items panel on the dashboard.
What is the Batch E5 ID and how is it different from a Claim ID?
The Batch E5 ID is the unique internal NEOS identifier for a batch — tracking all automation transactions for that batch. The Claim ID is the identifier for an individual claim record within a batch.
Why are there no documents showing for some batches in the Docs column?
Documents are only available when the automation workflow accessed and downloaded a batch file during processing. If claims were transmitted via direct integration, no documents will be present.
What does the Batch Parsing indicator mean?
The Batch Parsing icon confirms the automation successfully downloaded and parsed the batch file to extract claim data into NEOS. It is not clickable.
How do I find a specific patient's claim records?
Use the Search Patient Records bar in the Claims Status View to search by patient name, MRN, Member ID, or Claim ID. Or click directly on a patient name to open their Patient Detail Screen.
What should I do if I encounter a bug or something does not look right?
Contact the Element5 support team via the Support icon within the application or by emailing support@e5.ai.
